 Follow FBI charges lab owner who allegedly billed taxpayers $66M for 368K fake COVID tests
 Matt Durr Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:41 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The co-owner of an Illinois laboratory has been charged with five counts of wire fraud after he allegedly conducted a $66 million scheme involving fraudulent COVID-19 tests. According to the FBI , a grand jury returned an indictment Monday against 52-year-old Rajesh Patel of Schaumburg, Illinois.
 Patel is accused of submitting bills for hundreds of thousands of fake COVID-19 tests to the U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Uninsured Program. That program covered the costs of COVID-19 tests for individuals without health insurance.
 The scheme started in March 2021 when the lab entered into an agreement with Meridian Medical Staffing Inc. (Meridian). Patel's lab paid Meridian tens of millions of dollars to collect test specimens. Meridian also provided specimens and biological information of the purported patients.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, according to prosecutors, many of the patients that Patel submitted results for never actually existed or never provided test specimens to Meridian.
 Instead, Patel allegedly created fake "negative" test results for an estimated 368,000 PCR tests. The FBI says Patel's lab — located in Hillside, Illinois — submitted approximately $66.2 million in fraudulent claims to HRSA between May 2021 and April 2022.

 Advertisement Advertisement It's further alleged that HRSA paid the laboratory approximately $44.1 million and Patel personally obtained approximately $28 million in proceeds.
 Patel faces up to 20 years in prison on each of the five wire fraud counts
 "This defendant allegedly exploited a global crisis for personal gain, fabricating hundreds of thousands of COVID-19 tests – then billing the taxpayer for it," said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's Fraud Division. "Every dollar taken from a federal health care program is a dollar taken from the American people. The Fraud Division will find those who steal from taxpayers, and we will prosecute them."
